paragraphs.title: Choosing Aaron and the Holy Garments

easy.question: Whom does the Lord command Moses to bring near to serve as priests?
answers: Aaron and his sons
Moses and his sons
Only the skilled craftsmen
easy.explanation: The Lord commands Moses to bring Aaron and his sons near so that they may serve as priests.

easy.question: For whom are the holy garments intended?
answers: Moses alone
Aaron and his sons
All the Israelites
easy.explanation: The verses say that the holy garments are to be made for Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: Who is commanded to make Aaron’s garments?
answers: Aaron’s sons
Moses alone
The skilled craftsmen
easy.explanation: Moses is told to speak to the wise-hearted craftsmen, who will make Aaron’s garments.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence in these verses?
answers: Choosing Aaron and his sons, preparing the garments, making the holy garments
Preparing the garments, choosing Aaron, choosing the skilled craftsmen
Making the holy garments, choosing Aaron, naming the garments
medium.explanation: First Aaron and his sons are chosen for priestly service; then the garments are commanded; finally, their makers are identified.

medium.question: In the phrase “a broidered coat,” what does “broidered” describe?
answers: A garment with a patterned or woven design
A very long garment
A garment made of leather
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the kind of coat, indicating one made with an embroidered or patterned design.

medium.question: What purpose were the holy garments to serve?
answers: To give honor and beauty and set Aaron apart for priestly service
To distinguish Aaron by wealth from the Israelites
To enable Aaron to go to war
medium.explanation: The garments were for glory and beauty and were connected with Aaron’s consecration for priestly service.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom” about the skilled craftsmen?
answers: They were chosen only because they were Aaron’s sons
Their ability to make the garments was understood as wisdom given by God
They served as priests instead of Aaron
challenge.explanation: The verse connects their skill with a spirit of wisdom given by God.

challenge.question: Which item in the garment list might be missed when counting quickly?
answers: The girdle
The robe
The mitre
challenge.explanation: The list ends with “and a girdle,” an item that is easy to overlook.

challenge.question: What does the movement from speaking to the wise-hearted to making the garments show?
answers: The garments were made without planning
Making the holy garments required practical knowledge and skill
The craftsmen were responsible only for choosing the priests
challenge.explanation: The verses connect wisdom with actually carrying out the skilled work of making the garments.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom” about the skilled craftsmen?
answers: They were chosen only because they were Aaron’s sons
Their ability to make the garments was understood as wisdom given by God
They served as priests instead of Aaron
questions.explanation: The verse connects their skill with a spirit of wisdom given by God.

questions.question: Which item in the garment list might be missed when counting quickly?
answers: The girdle
The robe
The mitre
questions.explanation: The list ends with “and a girdle,” an item that is easy to overlook.

questions.question: What does the movement from speaking to the wise-hearted to making the garments show?
answers: The garments were made without planning
Making the holy garments required practical knowledge and skill
The craftsmen were responsible only for choosing the priests
questions.explanation: The verses connect wisdom with actually carrying out the skilled work of making the garments.

easy.question: Which materials are listed for making the ephod?
answers: Gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen
Silver, bronze, wood, and stone
Wool, leather, iron, and glass
easy.explanation: Verse 5 lists gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.

easy.question: What were they commanded to make from these materials?
answers: The altar
The ephod
The ark
easy.explanation: Verse 6 explicitly says, “They shall make the ephod.”

easy.question: How many shoulderpieces would the ephod have?
answers: One shoulderpiece
Three shoulderpieces
Two shoulderpieces
easy.explanation: Verse 7 speaks of two shoulderpieces joined together.

medium.question: What sequence is described in the verses?
answers: First the materials are taken, and then the ephod is made from them
First the ephod is worn, and then the materials are prepared
First the shoulderpieces are joined, and then only gold is gathered
medium.explanation: The materials are listed first, followed by instructions for making the ephod from them.

medium.question: In “fine twined linen,” what does “twined” describe?
answers: Shiny silver cloth
Linen that is twisted or woven together
Wool dyed red
medium.explanation: The phrase describes linen made by twisting or weaving its threads together.

medium.question: How is the ephod’s girdle described?
answers: It is made from the same materials and by the same kind of work as the ephod
It is made of gold alone
It is made of leather and is separate from the ephod
medium.explanation: The verse says the girdle is made “of the same” and according to the ephod’s work.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from describing the shoulderpieces as “joined”?
answers: They were separate pieces intended to be attached to the ephod
They were made from a completely different material
They served as a head covering
challenge.explanation: The shoulderpieces were separate sections joined to the ephod at its edges.

challenge.question: What quality of the workmanship is emphasized by “cunning work”?
answers: The ephod was made quickly and without planning
The ephod was made with careful, artistic skill
The ephod was made only from simple materials
challenge.explanation: “Cunning work” indicates planned and skillful craftsmanship.

challenge.question: Which detail strengthens the connection between the girdle and the ephod itself?
answers: The girdle is made only of blue
The girdle is placed only on the shoulderpieces
The girdle is made from the same materials and by the same work
challenge.explanation: The verse says the girdle is made according to the ephod’s work and from the same materials.

questions.question: What can be inferred from describing the shoulderpieces as “joined”?
answers: They were separate pieces intended to be attached to the ephod
They were made from a completely different material
They served as a head covering
questions.explanation: The shoulderpieces were separate sections joined to the ephod at its edges.

questions.question: What quality of the workmanship is emphasized by “cunning work”?
answers: The ephod was made quickly and without planning
The ephod was made with careful, artistic skill
The ephod was made only from simple materials
questions.explanation: “Cunning work” indicates planned and skillful craftsmanship.

questions.question: Which detail strengthens the connection between the girdle and the ephod itself?
answers: The girdle is made only of blue
The girdle is placed only on the shoulderpieces
The girdle is made from the same materials and by the same work
questions.explanation: The verse says the girdle is made according to the ephod’s work and from the same materials.

paragraphs.title: Memorial Stones on the Ephod’s Shoulders

easy.question: Whose names were to be engraved on the two onyx stones?
answers: The names of the children of Israel
The names of the priests
The names of the kings
easy.explanation: The verses command that the names of the children of Israel be engraved on the stones.

easy.question: How many onyx stones are mentioned?
answers: Three
Two
One
easy.explanation: The instructions call for two onyx stones.

easy.question: Where were the two stones to be placed?
answers: On Aaron’s head
On the altar
On the ephod’s shoulderpieces
easy.explanation: The stones were to be placed on the ephod’s shoulderpieces.

medium.question: How were the names of Israel’s children divided between the stones?
answers: Six names on each stone
All the names on one stone
One name on each stone
medium.explanation: Six names were to be placed on one stone and the remaining six on the other.

medium.question: What was the purpose of carrying Israel’s names on Aaron’s shoulders?
answers: To display Aaron’s wealth
To serve as a memorial before the Lord
To mark the location of the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The stones were memorial stones, and Aaron was to bear the names before the Lord.

medium.question: What are “ouches” in the phrase “set in ouches of gold”?
answers: Chains
Garments
Gold settings or frames
medium.explanation: The context shows that the stones were held in surrounding gold settings.

challenge.question: What order of actions is described in the verses?
answers: Engraving the names, placing the stones on the ephod, and attaching the chains
Attaching the chains, engraving the names, and placing the stones
Placing the stones, removing them, and then engraving the names
challenge.explanation: The names are engraved first, the stones are placed on the ephod, and the chains are then attached.

challenge.question: What does “according to their birth” indicate about the order of the names?
answers: They were arranged by size
They were arranged according to birth order
They were arranged randomly
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates an order connected with the tribes’ birth or family sequence.

challenge.question: What is the symbolic meaning of carrying Israel’s names on Aaron’s shoulders?
answers: The names were only decorative
The stones were used to count the priests
Aaron carried their memory and responsibility before the Lord
challenge.explanation: The memorial stones symbolize Aaron bearing Israel’s remembrance and representation before the Lord.

questions.question: What order of actions is described in the verses?
answers: Engraving the names, placing the stones on the ephod, and attaching the chains
Attaching the chains, engraving the names, and placing the stones
Placing the stones, removing them, and then engraving the names
questions.explanation: The names are engraved first, the stones are placed on the ephod, and the chains are then attached.

questions.question: What does “according to their birth” indicate about the order of the names?
answers: They were arranged by size
They were arranged according to birth order
They were arranged randomly
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates an order connected with the tribes’ birth or family sequence.

questions.question: What is the symbolic meaning of carrying Israel’s names on Aaron’s shoulders?
answers: The names were only decorative
The stones were used to count the priests
Aaron carried their memory and responsibility before the Lord
questions.explanation: The memorial stones symbolize Aaron bearing Israel’s remembrance and representation before the Lord.

paragraphs.title: The Breastplate of Judgment and Its Stones

easy.question: What was commanded to be made in these verses?
answers: The breastplate of judgment
A golden altar
A wooden ark
easy.explanation: The opening verse commands, “You shall make the breastplate of judgment.”

easy.question: What were the breastplate’s measurements?
answers: A cubit by a cubit
A span long and a span wide
Two cubits by a span
easy.explanation: The verse says it was a span in length and a span in width.

easy.question: How many rows of stones were on the breastplate?
answers: Two
Three
Four
easy.explanation: The verses describe four rows of stones.

medium.question: What was done after the breastplate’s shape was described?
answers: It was placed in the ark
It was painted blue
It was filled with rows of stones
medium.explanation: The instructions then say to set four rows of stones in it.

medium.question: In context, what does “settings of stones” mean?
answers: Broken stones
Stones set securely in their places
Stones kept outside the breastplate
medium.explanation: The context describes stones arranged in rows and set in gold settings.

medium.question: How did the number of stones relate to the tribes of Israel?
answers: There were twelve stones for the twelve tribes
There were four stones for the four patriarchs
There were seven stones for the seven days
medium.explanation: The breastplate had twelve stones, one for each tribe of Israel.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from having three stones in each of four rows?
answers: There were twelve stones altogether
There were four stones altogether
There were seven stones altogether
challenge.explanation: Four rows of three stones make twelve stones in total.

challenge.question: What does “every one with his name” emphasize?
answers: The stones had no names
Each tribe had a stone bearing its name
Only Moses’ name was written
challenge.explanation: Each stone represented one tribe and bore that tribe’s name.

challenge.question: What does “foursquare it shall be, being doubled” indicate?
answers: The breastplate was round and open
The breastplate was made from one stone
The breastplate was square and doubled or folded
challenge.explanation: The wording describes both its square shape and its doubled construction.

questions.question: What can be inferred from having three stones in each of four rows?
answers: There were twelve stones altogether
There were four stones altogether
There were seven stones altogether
questions.explanation: Four rows of three stones make twelve stones in total.

questions.question: What does “every one with his name” emphasize?
answers: The stones had no names
Each tribe had a stone bearing its name
Only Moses’ name was written
questions.explanation: Each stone represented one tribe and bore that tribe’s name.

questions.question: What does “foursquare it shall be, being doubled” indicate?
answers: The breastplate was round and open
The breastplate was made from one stone
The breastplate was square and doubled or folded
questions.explanation: The wording describes both its square shape and its doubled construction.

paragraphs.title: Attaching the Breastplate to the Ephod

easy.question: What were the chains on the breastplate made of?
answers: Pure gold
Silver
Bronze
easy.explanation: The verses specify chains of pure gold.

easy.question: How many gold rings were placed at the ends of the breastplate?
answers: Four
Two
Six
easy.explanation: The instructions call for two gold rings.

easy.question: With what cord was the breastplate fastened to the ephod?
answers: A red cord
A white cord
A blue cord
easy.explanation: The breastplate was fastened with a blue cord.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the rings and cords described here?
answers: To attach the breastplate to the ephod
To decorate the mitre
To hold the breastplate stones in their settings
medium.explanation: The rings, chains, and cords kept the breastplate attached to the ephod.

medium.question: Why were additional rings placed on the ephod’s shoulderpieces?
answers: To hang the robe from them
To attach the breastplate to them
To hold the ephod’s stones
medium.explanation: The rings on the shoulderpieces were used to connect the breastplate.

medium.question: In “the breastplate be not loosed from the ephod,” what does “loosed” mean?
answers: Moved or separated
Shined
Tore
medium.explanation: The context shows that the breastplate was not to move away from or detach from the ephod.

challenge.question: Which sequence correctly describes how the breastplate was attached to the ephod?
answers: Rings on the breastplate, chains, rings on the ephod, and blue cords
Blue cords, breastplate stones, chains, and rings
Rings on the ephod, ephod stones, chains, and cords
challenge.explanation: The instructions proceed from the breastplate’s rings to the chains, the ephod’s rings, and the blue cords.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command that the breastplate not be loosed from the ephod?
answers: The breastplate was placed inside the ephod
The breastplate and ephod were to remain firmly connected
The breastplate was made from the same material as the ephod
challenge.explanation: The command emphasizes stability and continued attachment.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the attachment was planned at both the upper and lower parts of the ephod?
answers: The mention of pure gold alone
The command to make two chains
The mention of the shoulderpieces and the ephod’s girdle
challenge.explanation: The shoulderpieces are above, while the girdle marks the lower connection area.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes how the breastplate was attached to the ephod?
answers: Rings on the breastplate, chains, rings on the ephod, and blue cords
Blue cords, breastplate stones, chains, and rings
Rings on the ephod, ephod stones, chains, and cords
questions.explanation: The instructions proceed from the breastplate’s rings to the chains, the ephod’s rings, and the blue cords.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command that the breastplate not be loosed from the ephod?
answers: The breastplate was placed inside the ephod
The breastplate and ephod were to remain firmly connected
The breastplate was made from the same material as the ephod
questions.explanation: The command emphasizes stability and continued attachment.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the attachment was planned at both the upper and lower parts of the ephod?
answers: The mention of pure gold alone
The command to make two chains
The mention of the shoulderpieces and the ephod’s girdle
questions.explanation: The shoulderpieces are above, while the girdle marks the lower connection area.

paragraphs.title: Aaron Carries Israel on His Heart

easy.question: What did Aaron carry in the breastplate of judgment?
answers: The names of the children of Israel
The tabernacle vessels
The book of the law
easy.explanation: The verse says Aaron bore the names of the children of Israel.

easy.question: Where did Aaron carry Israel’s names?
answers: On his head
On his heart
On his hand
easy.explanation: The names were carried on Aaron’s heart.

easy.question: Before whom were Israel’s names to be remembered?
answers: Before the people
Before Moses
Before the Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says they were a memorial before the Lord.

medium.question: When did Aaron carry Israel’s names on his heart?
answers: When he entered the holy place
When he left the camp
During construction of the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The verse connects this action with Aaron’s entering the holy place.

medium.question: What was the purpose of carrying the names on the breastplate?
answers: To display the priestly garments
To serve as a memorial before the Lord
To count the tribes of Israel
medium.explanation: The stated purpose was to keep the names as a memorial before the Lord.

medium.question: In “for a memorial before the Lord,” what does “memorial” mean?
answers: Something intended to be remembered
Something meant to disappear
Something intended for judgment
medium.explanation: A memorial is something that serves to bring people or events to remembrance.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “on his heart”?
answers: The names were hidden inside the garment
The names were close and important to him
The names were written on his hand
challenge.explanation: The heart symbolizes closeness and importance, emphasizing Aaron’s connection with Israel.

challenge.question: Which word emphasizes that the memorial was not a one-time event?
answers: Continually
Holy place
Breastplate
challenge.explanation: “Continually” indicates an ongoing remembrance before the Lord.

challenge.question: What idea sequence appears in the verse?
answers: Aaron enters the holy place, and Israel’s names are carried as a memorial
Israel’s names are carried so Aaron can build the holy place
Aaron leaves the holy place and then writes the names
challenge.explanation: The verse connects Aaron’s entering the holy place with carrying Israel’s names as a memorial.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “on his heart”?
answers: The names were hidden inside the garment
The names were close and important to him
The names were written on his hand
questions.explanation: The heart symbolizes closeness and importance, emphasizing Aaron’s connection with Israel.

questions.question: Which word emphasizes that the memorial was not a one-time event?
answers: Continually
Holy place
Breastplate
questions.explanation: “Continually” indicates an ongoing remembrance before the Lord.

questions.question: What idea sequence appears in the verse?
answers: Aaron enters the holy place, and Israel’s names are carried as a memorial
Israel’s names are carried so Aaron can build the holy place
Aaron leaves the holy place and then writes the names
questions.explanation: The verse connects Aaron’s entering the holy place with carrying Israel’s names as a memorial.

paragraphs.title: The Urim and Thummim and Israel’s Judgment

easy.question: What was to be placed in the breastplate of judgment?
answers: The Urim and the Thummim
Moses’ staff
The tablets of the covenant
easy.explanation: The verse commands that the Urim and Thummim be placed in the breastplate.

easy.question: On whose heart were the Urim and Thummim to be placed?
answers: Moses’ heart
Aaron’s heart
The Israelites’ hearts
easy.explanation: The verse says they would be upon Aaron’s heart.

easy.question: Before whom would Aaron come with the Urim and Thummim on his heart?
answers: Before Pharaoh
Before the Israelites
Before the Lord
easy.explanation: Aaron would come before the Lord with them upon his heart.

medium.question: What does it mean that Aaron carried Israel’s judgment on his heart?
answers: He carried the sanctuary vessels in his hands
He represented Israel before the Lord
He taught Israel the law
medium.explanation: Carrying Israel’s judgment on his heart describes representing them before the Lord.

medium.question: What sequence is described in the verse?
answers: Aaron carries Israel’s judgment, and then the Urim are placed in the breastplate
Israel comes before the Lord, and then Aaron puts on the breastplate
The Urim and Thummim are placed in the breastplate, and they are on Aaron’s heart when he comes before the Lord
medium.explanation: The verse first commands placing the Urim and Thummim in the breastplate and then describes Aaron before the Lord.

medium.question: In “Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel,” what does “judgment” mean?
answers: Israel’s case and concerns
A special garment of Aaron
Israel’s journey
medium.explanation: In context, “judgment” refers to Israel’s case or concerns carried before the Lord.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “continually” at the end of the verse?
answers: Aaron’s representation of Israel before the Lord was ongoing
It happened only once
The Urim and Thummim were used only during war
challenge.explanation: “Continually” emphasizes that Aaron’s representation was not a one-time act.

challenge.question: What is the relationship between “on Aaron’s heart” and “before the Lord”?
answers: Aaron wore the breastplate only when far from the sanctuary
Aaron carried Israel’s concerns into the Lord’s presence
Aaron hid Israel from the Lord
challenge.explanation: Together, the phrases show Aaron representing Israel before the Lord.

challenge.question: Which wording shows that Aaron carried Israel’s concerns, not merely an object?
answers: The verse mentions the breastplate
The verse mentions the Urim
The verse says, “Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart”
challenge.explanation: The explicit phrase describes the symbolic carrying of Israel’s concerns.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “continually” at the end of the verse?
answers: Aaron’s representation of Israel before the Lord was ongoing
It happened only once
The Urim and Thummim were used only during war
questions.explanation: “Continually” emphasizes that Aaron’s representation was not a one-time act.

questions.question: What is the relationship between “on Aaron’s heart” and “before the Lord”?
answers: Aaron wore the breastplate only when far from the sanctuary
Aaron carried Israel’s concerns into the Lord’s presence
Aaron hid Israel from the Lord
questions.explanation: Together, the phrases show Aaron representing Israel before the Lord.

questions.question: Which wording shows that Aaron carried Israel’s concerns, not merely an object?
answers: The verse mentions the breastplate
The verse mentions the Urim
The verse says, “Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart”
questions.explanation: The explicit phrase describes the symbolic carrying of Israel’s concerns.

paragraphs.title: The Blue Robe of the Ephod

easy.question: What garment was Moses commanded to make?
answers: The robe of the ephod
The priestly girdle
The golden plate
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly commands the making of the robe of the ephod.

easy.question: What color was the robe to be?
answers: Purple
Blue
White
easy.explanation: The robe was to be entirely blue.

easy.question: What was not to happen to the robe?
answers: It was not to get wet
It was not to be stained
It was not to be torn
easy.explanation: The verse says, “It shall not be rent.”

medium.question: Why was a binding made around the robe’s opening?
answers: To strengthen the opening and prevent tearing
To change the robe’s color
To shorten the robe
medium.explanation: The reinforced opening was intended to keep the robe from tearing.

medium.question: In “a binding of woven work round about the hole,” what is a “binding”?
answers: A spoken language
A reinforced edge or border
A special color
medium.explanation: The context describes a reinforced border around the neck opening.

medium.question: What detail appears first in the description of the robe?
answers: The command to make it and its color
The warning not to tear it
The binding around the opening
medium.explanation: The verse first states that the robe is to be made entirely blue, then describes its opening and binding.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “there shall be an hole in the top of it”?
answers: The robe had no opening
The opening was at the top of the robe
The opening was at the bottom
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies an opening at the top for the head.

challenge.question: What is the robe’s opening compared to?
answers: An opening in a tent
The edge of a cloak
The opening of a coat of mail
challenge.explanation: The verse compares it to the opening of a coat of mail.

challenge.question: Which connection best explains the ending “that it be not rent”?
answers: The opening had a woven binding around it, strengthening it
The robe was blue, so it could not tear
The robe was short, so it could not tear
challenge.explanation: The woven binding reinforced the opening and helped prevent tearing.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “there shall be an hole in the top of it”?
answers: The robe had no opening
The opening was at the top of the robe
The opening was at the bottom
questions.explanation: The verse identifies an opening at the top for the head.

questions.question: What is the robe’s opening compared to?
answers: An opening in a tent
The edge of a cloak
The opening of a coat of mail
questions.explanation: The verse compares it to the opening of a coat of mail.

questions.question: Which connection best explains the ending “that it be not rent”?
answers: The opening had a woven binding around it, strengthening it
The robe was blue, so it could not tear
The robe was short, so it could not tear
questions.explanation: The woven binding reinforced the opening and helped prevent tearing.

paragraphs.title: Pomegranates and Bells on the Robe’s Hem

easy.question: What was placed on the robe’s hem?
answers: Pomegranates and golden bells
Crowns and chains
Stones and silver vessels
easy.explanation: The verses place pomegranates and golden bells around the robe’s hem.

easy.question: What colors were the pomegranates?
answers: Gold, silver, and bronze
Blue, purple, and scarlet
White, black, and green
easy.explanation: The pomegranates were made of blue, purple, and scarlet.

easy.question: Who wore the robe?
answers: Moses
The Israelites
Aaron
easy.explanation: The robe was to be upon Aaron as he ministered.

medium.question: How were the golden bells and pomegranates arranged?
answers: A golden bell and a pomegranate alternately
All the bells on one side
All the pomegranates in the center
medium.explanation: The verse gives the repeating pattern: a golden bell and a pomegranate.

medium.question: What does “upon the hem” mean here?
answers: On the top of the robe
On the edge or lower border of the robe
On the sleeves of the robe
medium.explanation: The hem is the robe’s lower edge, which the items surrounded.

medium.question: When would Aaron’s sound be heard?
answers: Only while sleeping
Only when speaking to the people
When entering the holy place and when coming out
medium.explanation: The verse connects the sound with both Aaron’s entrance and exit.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated pattern “a golden bell and a pomegranate”?
answers: The pomegranates were only on the front
The bells and pomegranates formed a repeating pattern around the hem
There was only one bell on the robe
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording indicates an alternating pattern around the robe.

challenge.question: What does “when he goeth in … and when he cometh out” emphasize?
answers: The sound was heard only before entering
The sound was heard only after leaving
The sound was heard both on entering and on leaving the holy place
challenge.explanation: The phrase names both opposite moments: entering and leaving.

challenge.question: What is the main connection between the bells and Aaron’s service?
answers: They were part of his ministering garments, and their sound was connected with his not dying
They were only decorative
They called the people to gather
challenge.explanation: The bells were part of Aaron’s service before the Lord, and the verse connects their sound with his safety.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repeated pattern “a golden bell and a pomegranate”?
answers: The pomegranates were only on the front
The bells and pomegranates formed a repeating pattern around the hem
There was only one bell on the robe
questions.explanation: The repeated wording indicates an alternating pattern around the robe.

questions.question: What does “when he goeth in … and when he cometh out” emphasize?
answers: The sound was heard only before entering
The sound was heard only after leaving
The sound was heard both on entering and on leaving the holy place
questions.explanation: The phrase names both opposite moments: entering and leaving.

questions.question: What is the main connection between the bells and Aaron’s service?
answers: They were part of his ministering garments, and their sound was connected with his not dying
They were only decorative
They called the people to gather
questions.explanation: The bells were part of Aaron’s service before the Lord, and the verse connects their sound with his safety.

paragraphs.title: The Golden Plate on Aaron’s Forehead

easy.question: What was the plate made of?
answers: Pure gold
Pure silver
Bronze
easy.explanation: The verse commands a plate of pure gold.

easy.question: Where was the plate placed?
answers: On the chest
On the mitre
On the shoulder
easy.explanation: It was placed on the front of the mitre.

easy.question: What was engraved on the plate?
answers: Aaron the priest
